maria: Heads up — intermittent hang in python SDK async stream when backend closes right after sending a newline-only SSE final chunk. Generator never completes sometimes.

maria: Minimal repro (async):
```py
agen = client.stream_chat(model="mini")
async for msg in agen:
    if msg.get("done"):
        break
```

sam: Which HTTP client? aiohttp or httpx? any proxies/ingress in front?

maria: aiohttp, nginx ingress. No custom retry. Happens under bursty traffic.

leo: I saw this — parser expects an explicit empty-line delimiter. If read() returns b'' (EOF) before we hit the delimiter, we don't synthesize the last event. That leaves the async iterator waiting.

sam: Can users force-close the stream? Does agen.aclose() forward to the transport?

maria: Tried await agen.aclose() and it hung. Cancelling the task leaves socket refs in the loop.

leo: Short-term fixes: treat EOF as equivalent to empty-line (emit final event), and add a small read safeguard/timeout at transport layer. Longer-term: provide a Stream object with explicit cancel()/close() for sync+async clients so cancellation isn't implicit.

ops-bot: CI: test_stream_cancel flaky on linux-aio (FAILED) — rerun scheduled.

sam: Filing INF-4123 to track infra/CI flakes and assign to eng-runtime.

maria: Workaround for users: wrap iteration in asyncio.wait_for and call agen.aclose() in finally. Not great but unblocks.

leo: I'll open a small PR to handle EOF-as-empty-line and add unit tests for (a) final chunk is "\n" + FIN and (b) final read returns b'' with no newline. Will also add a changelog note about aclose semantics.

maria: Thanks — please ping here when PR is up and I'll validate against our ingress config.
